title: Gate primary-form repair with isolated component overlays
preconditions: A source reference has an identifiable component ROI or a separable material/value range.
The Blender candidate component can be rendered in isolation with alpha.
The view correspondence is documented; perspective uncertainty remains explicit.
procedure: Declare reference and candidate ROIs for each identity-critical component before secondary-detail work.
Create an isolated component mask; use alpha for the candidate and a documented luminance/ROI mask or other explicit segmentation for the reference.
Compare a strict frame when placement is meaningful. Use uniform-bbox only to remove translation and overall scale while preserving aspect ratio.
Inspect the overlay and contour heatmap, then localize the failure to primary silhouette, proportion, negative space, or view mismatch.
If the primary silhouette is wrong, replace or rebuild the component cage through a recoverable operation instead of adding cosmetic detail around it.
prohibitions: Do not use whole-object IoU as evidence that a small identity-critical component is accurate.
Do not use independently stretched bbox alignment to claim correct proportions.
Do not turn a single target's metrics into a universal promotion threshold.

evidence.observed_failure: Whole-object normalized scores near 0.77–0.88 concealed component overlap of 0.4001 for the spout, 0.5741 for the handle, and 0.5156 for the base.

limitations: ROI and luminance segmentation are currently explicit human/modeler inputs, not automatic semantic segmentation.
The comparison does not calibrate photographic perspective or hidden geometry.
One rejected asset proves the diagnostic need, not transfer success; reproduce on an unrelated target before broader promotion.
